candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this table presents enforceable discharge or instream limits versus background screening or fact-sheet illustration determines if any numeric values here are selected as applicable limits for compliance comparison.

Interpretation of Ce as an effluent concentration input and 2.13*Ce as a derived acute aquatic criterion changes which numeric limit is applied when effluent measurements exist for pollutants with populated Ce cells.
Different readings of which domestic-supply, chronic aquatic, or human-health column governs effluent compliance would change the selected enforceable limit for the same pollutant and measurement.

Whether MQL is treated as a reporting floor, a method detection limit, or a compliance comparison threshold affects whether reported values below MQL can be compared to limits (A) and whether absent or below-quantitation results are documented no-data versus inadequate evidence (C).

This row supplies a nonzero Ce (10 ug/l), derived acute value (21.3), and multiple finite aquatic and human-health criteria (19, 15, 30) alongside 1E+100 placeholders; choosing among these numbers changes the applicable limit for pentachlorophenol measurements.

Ce=2.11 and small derived chronic/human-health values coexist with Domestic Criteria 10500 and Human Health Criteria 860000; different criterion-selection rules yield very different applicable limits for phenol.

Only three pollutants in the segment carry populated Ce values; treating this row's Ce-derived limits versus its Domestic Criteria value of 6 ug/l changes the enforceable limit applied to DEHP measurements.

Blank Ce with zero acute/chronic/human-health derived columns but nonzero Domestic Criteria (70) and Human Health Criteria (5300) raises whether a zero-derived limit applies, no aquatic limit applies, or a different criteria column governs.

Whether 1E+100 denotes no numeric criterion, a non-operative placeholder, or an effectively unbounded limit determines if compliance comparison is applicable for parameters whose aquatic or irrigation columns show this value.

This row lacks an MQL entry while listing finite chronic aquatic (28) and acute aquatic (6.6) criteria; interpretation affects both which limit applies (A) and how missing or sub-quantitation nonylphenol results are classified without a stated MQL (C).

The Need TMDL column header signals whether TMDL-based limits may supersede or supplement the tabulated criteria; all rows show N/A, and whether that forecloses TMDL-driven limits changes limit selection.

This analyte-group label may delimit which base/neutral organic monitoring is required as a suite; treating it as operative scope versus descriptive grouping changes which monitoring obligations are considered applicable.
